label: Phase-out mondial des gaz fluorés à effet de serre (Amendement de Kigali étendu)

sources: IPCC AR6 SYR Figure 4.4 — F-gas reduction represents ~1.5 GtCO2eq/yr mitigation potential by 2030 at very low cost
UNEP Kigali Amendment Assessment 2023 — Full implementation could avoid up to 0.5°C warming by 2100
Climate & Clean Air Coalition — HFC replacement with low-GWP alternatives (HFOs, CO2, ammonia) is technically mature in all major application sectors
UNEP Kigali Assessment 2023 — Full Kigali implementation avoids 0.3–0.5°C of warming by 2100

planetary_limits.note: Some HFO replacements degrade to PFAS ('forever chemicals') in the environment

societal_indicators.note: Accelerated transfer of low-GWP refrigerant technologies to developing nations

interactions.note: Building renovation increases heat pump deployment which uses refrigerants; phase-out ensures low-GWP refrigerants in new equipment

methodological_note: Lowest uncertainty (score 1) of all policies in the catalogue — substitute refrigerants are commercially available, phaseout technology is mature, and Kigali Amendment already covers 197 parties. Median impact of 1.5 GtCO2eq/yr at full effect (2036) is consistent with IPCC AR6 SYR Fig 4.4. Uncertainty arises from: (1) challenge of phasing out PFCs and SF6 in semiconductor manufacturing, (2) air conditioning demand growth in developing nations partially offsetting reductions. GWP-weighted emissions decline rapidly in first 12 years then stabilise. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
